eligibility.label: Resources are separate from price
eligibility.text: Provide a sworn affidavit declaring at least US$350,000 in financial resources, with supporting resources/source-of-funds documents under amended section 36(1A). This is not an additional government fee or a replacement for the NEF contribution.

eligibility.label: Qualifying dependants
eligibility.text: Act 22/2025 includes a spouse; the applicant’s or spouse’s children aged 21 or below, or no more than 30 and fully supported; parents of either spouse above 55 and fully supported; and the applicant’s unmarried siblings below 18 with parental/guardian consent. It also includes fully supported people of any age with physical or mental disabilities, with additional incapacity, care and support evidence. Assess each person individually.

eligibility.label: Prior refusals and disclosure
eligibility.text: Amended section 36 requires denial after a visa refusal by a country with which Saint Lucia has visa-free travel unless the applicant subsequently obtained a visa to that country. A citizenship-by-investment denial by an OECS member state is a separate discretionary denial ground. Disclose refusals and obtain case-specific advice; paying the qualifying amount does not cure ineligibility.

eligibility.label: Built property: enacted, with an availability check
eligibility.text: Regulation 10A and the amended schedules create a distinct US$500,000 approved built-property route for the applicant and qualifying dependants, with a US$30,000 applicant administration fee plus other charges. The Board must publish an approved project in the Gazette. This review did not establish a gazetted project with functioning intake and available inventory for this route. Obtain those records before treating a particular property as available. The separate regulation 10 cutoff concerns new developer project-approval applications after 1 December 2025; it does not establish closure of all previously approved projects.

routeOptions.availability: Project intake and inventory not established by this review

afterApproval.label: Successful applicants: biometrics
afterApproval.text: Regulation 15A requires successful applicants to provide biometric data, including fingerprints and other identifying characteristics. The reviewed instrument does not specify an appointment location, deadline or collection fee; obtain current Unit instructions.

afterApproval.label: Residency and genuine link
afterApproval.text: Section 30A applies prescribed residency and genuine-link requirements to the applicant and each qualifying dependant from 1 January 2026. Neither Act 22/2025 nor S.I. 57/2026 supplies a universal day count. The reviewed programme guidance does not resolve the detailed prescription or its application to individual pending files. Obtain the applicable instrument and instructions before planning visits.

afterApproval.label: Built property: hold and title steps
afterApproval.text: Keep the qualifying investment for at least five years after citizenship. Within 90 days after receiving the citizenship certificate, take the necessary steps to obtain title/ownership documents, including registering the land interest or completing and recording the share transfer/issue. This is a deadline to take steps, not a universal deadline to complete final title. It does not apply to NEF contributions or bonds.

afterApproval.label: Built property: proof and consequences
afterApproval.text: Give the Unit proof of the acquired interest, such as the Land Register or share ownership, within the period the Unit specifies. If unable to supply it in that period, apply for an extension of no more than 30 days. Regulation 10A(14) gives the Minister power to revoke the registration certificate and requires its surrender; obtain advice about compliance and any Unit notice. A five-year resale plan does not remove these earlier duties.

afterApproval.label: National Action Bonds: keep the issue record
afterApproval.text: The published NAB option requires registration in the applicant’s name for five years from first issue; it is non-interest-bearing. Keep the issue and payment records and obtain the actual redemption terms. Redemption at maturity is different from a refund following withdrawal or refusal.

afterApproval.label: Names and passport applications
afterApproval.text: Section 36A restricts name changes for five years after the registration certificate, with documented exceptions for family-status changes, protective programmes and clerical/transliteration correction by the Unit or competent authority. Where a name changes, the Act requires written notice to the Unit before a passport application, with the prescribed evidence and due-diligence fee. Obtain instructions for your exception and renewal; the biometric amendment does not establish a renewal calendar or fee here. Passport expiry is separate from loss of citizenship.

afterApproval.label: Passport renewal: use the applicable consular channel
afterApproval.text: The Saint Lucia embassy in Taipei publishes CBI-specific renewal instructions: initial document verification, then an appointment, with original documents submitted in person or by registered mail under its overseas procedure. Its current page warns of substantial passport-processing delays. This describes that embassy’s channel; confirm the applicable mission, document list and current charges for your residence. It does not establish where the new statutory biometrics are collected, and the earlier 30-day return time is not a current delivery promise.

paymentRisk.label: NEF submission and qualifying payment
paymentRisk.text: The current investment page labels processing and due-diligence fees at submission non-refundable, and says the NEF qualifying contribution follows approval. The portal also states fees and qualifying investments paid are non-refundable. Do not assume withdrawal or rejection recovers paid amounts.

paymentRisk.label: Built-property payments and escrow
paymentRisk.text: Regulation 10A requires the agreement, proof of the qualifying payment and value evidence with the application. This differs from the NEF payment sequence. Regulations 12A–12C require approved escrow arrangements with written release, rights, obligations, remuneration and applicable construction-drawdown terms. Obtain the executed agreements and independent advice on refusal, withdrawal, title failure and default; escrow is not an automatic refund guarantee.
